B) Cp declines monoexponentially; V = Dose/C0; t½ = 0.693/k
C) Two-compartment means zero distribution time and single exponential only
D) Oral absorption is always zero-order with constant mg/h for every immediate-release tablet
extreme.answer: B) Cp declines monoexponentially; V = Dose/C0; t½ = 0.693/k
extreme.explanation: Instant mixing assumption yields monoexponential decline for 1-compartment models. Therefore, the most accurate choice is: Cp declines monoexponentially; V = Dose/C0; t½ = 0.693/k. One-compartment is the simplest mixing assumption.

extreme.question: A rapidly progressive presentation of two-compartment model is reviewed with more than one plausible explanation. Which of the following is most likely?
options: A) IV bolus always shows multi-exponential tissue distribution with no simple V
B) Distribution phase (α) then elimination phase (β) after IV bolus
C) Two-compartment means zero distribution time and single exponential only
D) Oral absorption is always zero-order with constant mg/h for every immediate-release tablet

extreme.explanation: Drug equilibrates between central and peripheral compartments. Therefore, the most accurate choice is: Distribution phase (α) then elimination phase (β) after IV bolus. Biexponential decline is expected, not monoexponential only.
